bounded_statement: Within the supplied files of case:d8e451762e6f79802f9f, the selected result (exact two-sided binomial test, 15/20 uv_bright first visits, p = 0.041389, declared significant at the 5% level) is produced by entering all 20 release rows as independent Bernoulli observations even though the declared independent unit is forager_id and the 20 rows come from only 6 foragers with 2–4 rows each. The row-independent binomial procedure therefore receives repeated entries per independent unit, and the significance claim does not hold under a unit-respecting reanalysis of the same data (per-forager majority sign test: 4 of 5 non-tied foragers favor uv_bright, two-sided p = 0.375).

counterevidence_considered.description: The report openly discloses the repeated-measures structure in its Notes section, acknowledging that several rows describe the same insect and that the test weighs each row as one independent draw. This is transparency about the limitation, but it is not a mitigation: no unit-level aggregation, mixed model, or other dependence-aware procedure was applied, and the significance claim in the selected result is stated unconditionally.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the finding in three ways. (1) Could each row legitimately be an independent unit? No: the data description explicitly names forager_id as the independent-unit column and states that most bees appear several times; the CSV confirms 6 distinct forager_id values across 20 rows (e.g., FOR-01 on rows for T001, T007, T013, T018). (2) Does the workflow anywhere adjust for or aggregate over foragers before testing? No: main() sets total = len(trials) and bright to the row-level uv_bright count and passes these directly to binomtest; the per-forager tally is used only for a descriptive table. (3) Is the issue immaterial, i.e., would the conclusion survive a unit-respecting analysis? No: recomputing from the report's own per-forager table, 4 of 5 non-tied foragers show a uv_bright majority (FOR-06 is tied at 1/2), giving an exact two-sided sign test p = 2 × (C(5,4)+C(5,5))/2^5 = 0.375, and the per-forager mean of within-forager uv_bright shares (0.736) rests on only 6 units; the reported 5%-level significance therefore depends on treating the 20 dependent rows as independent. I also verified the reported counts (15/20; per-forager 4/4, 3/4, 4/4, 2/3, 1/3, 1/2 sums to 15/20) and that binomtest(15, 20, 0.5) yields p ≈ 0.0414 as reported, so the issue is in the design of the test entry, not an arithmetic error. All falsification attempts failed, so the issue stands.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py counts every CSV row as one Bernoulli trial (total = len(trials); bright = row-level count) and submits the pooled row-level counts to scipy.stats.binomtest(bright, total, 0.5), a procedure whose validity assumes each of the n entries is an independent draw. Because the data-description designates forager_id as the independent unit and each forager contributes 2–4 rows, repeated non-independent observations from the same unit are entered as if independent, inflating the effective sample size from 6 units to 20 rows and deflating the reported p-value on which the significance conclusion rests.
